prompt: Main thread, ticket-review, SIMPLE ticket TL-33 (unknown CLI commands should say which command was not recognized). One logical change in src/cli.js plus its test; the existing unknown-command test needs updating. The simulated user approves whatever plan is presented.
expected_output: Sizes it SIMPLE, presents a short plan and one task file for a single approval, implements in the main thread after approval, then dispatches one fresh pr-review that re-runs the acceptance commands and build/test. One subagent in total.
invocation: The developer typed `/ticket-review` followed by a message, which invokes the `ticket-review` skill with that message.

user_script.approval: Approved - I agree with your recommendations.
user_script.question: Follow your recommendation.

assertions.text: The first reply sizes the ticket SIMPLE
Changes no source or test file before the user approves
Needs exactly one approval from the user before implementation starts
Implements in the main thread: no execute-task subagent
Starts exactly one subagent in the whole run, and it is the pr-review
The pr-review subagent itself re-runs an acceptance command (the mistyped command) and the test suite
Final behavior is right: an unknown command prints `Unknown command: <name>` then the usage; no command prints the usage alone; known commands are unchanged
The run's tests fail against the original src/cli.js
Build, test and lint pass on the final tree
A task file for the change is written under docs/tasks/feature-TL-33-unknown-command/ with a runnable acceptance command
Before implementing, shows the user a short plan to approve: what changes, how acceptance is checked, and what stays out
